extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and examiners preparing or reviewing nucleotide/amino acid sequence disclosures and biological-material deposits for U.S. patent filings
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and formatting standards for (1) biological-material deposits needed for patent enablement and (2) nucleotide/amino acid sequence disclosures and Sequence Listings in U.S. patent applications (rules both for pre‑July 1, 2022 ST.25-based submissions and for on/after July 1, 2022 ST.26 XML submissions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner rejection for missing or unacceptable deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: If a deposit is needed and has not been made, replaced, or supplemented in accordance with these regulations, the examiner, where appropriate, shall reject the affected claims under the appropriate provision of 35 U.S.C. 112, explaining why a deposit is needed and/or why a deposit actually made cannot be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must reply by making an acceptable original, replacement, or supplemental deposit, assuring in writing that an acceptable deposit will be made, requesting a certificate of correction (if patent owner), or arguing why a deposit is not needed or why the deposit should be accepted. Other replies are nonresponsive; rejection repeated until satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three‑month allowability period for promised deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application is otherwise in condition for allowance except for a needed deposit and the Office has received a written assurance that an acceptable deposit will be made, the Office may notify the applicant in a notice of allowability and set a three‑month period from the mailing date of the notice within which the deposit must be made to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This three‑month period is not extendable under § 1.136 (see § 1.136(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification must contain deposit identifying information
rubrics_metrics.description: For each deposit made pursuant to these regulations, the specification shall contain: (1) the accession number for the deposit; (2) the date of the deposit; (3) a description of the deposited biological material sufficient to specifically identify it and to permit examination; and (4) the name and address of the depository.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any amendment required to add accession number, deposit date, or depository name/address must be filed before or with payment of the issue fee (see § 1.312).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed replies to examiner on deposit issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant/patent owner must either: (1) make an acceptable original, replacement, or supplemental deposit or assure the Office in writing that one will be made (or request certificate of correction for patents meeting § 1.805 requirements), or (2) argue why a deposit is not needed and/or why an actual deposit should be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other replies are considered nonresponsive; examiner will repeat rejection until compliant or convinced deposit is unnecessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of nucleotide/amino acid sequences (pre‑ST.26 rule applicability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nucleotide and/or amino acid sequences (for §§ 1.821–1.825 applicability) mean an unbranched sequence of 4 or more amino acids or an unbranched sequence of 10 or more nucleotides; branched sequences and sequences with fewer than these 'specifically defined' residues are excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Specifically defined' excludes Xaa (amino acids) and 'n' (nucleotides); appendices A–F contain symbol tables from WIPO ST.25.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbols/code set for sequences (pre‑ST.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: The code for representing nucleotide and/or amino acid sequence characters shall conform to the code set forth in appendices A and C to this subpart; no other code shall be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modified bases/amino acids may be presented as corresponding unmodified residues only if listed in appendices B/D and the modification is set forth in the Feature section; otherwise use 'n' or 'Xaa' and provide feature keys per appendices E/F.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive conformity to §§1.821–1.825 for sequence presentation (pre‑ST.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applications containing nucleotide and/or amino acid sequences must, with regard to the manner in which sequences are presented and described, conform exclusively to the requirements of §§ 1.821 through 1.825.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not mix other formats or informal representations for sequences in the application; follow the precise rules below for Sequence Listing content and format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for a separate 'Sequence Listing' part
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications containing nucleotide/amino acid sequences must contain a 'Sequence Listing,' which is a separate part of the specification containing each sequence and associated information using the symbols and format required by §§ 1.822 and 1.823.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'Sequence Listing' must be submitted as (1) an ASCII plain text file in compliance with § 1.824, (2) a PDF via the USPTO electronic filing system, or (3) on physical sheets of paper, subject to additional CRF and incorporation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referencing sequences in description, claims, or drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the description or claims discuss a sequence that is set forth in the 'Sequence Listing,' reference must be made to the sequence by use of the sequence identifier (preceded by 'SEQ ID NO:' or the like) in the text of the description or claims, even if the sequence is also embedded in the text; when in drawings, use the sequence identifier either in the drawing or in the Brief Description where correlation is clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence identifiers must match those assigned in the Sequence Listing (§ 1.823(a)(5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: CRF requirement when Sequence Listing submitted as PDF/paper (pre‑ST.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Sequence Listing is submitted as a PDF file or on physical sheets (instead of ASCII), a CRF (computer readable form) of the Sequence Listing must be submitted in accordance with § 1.824, and a statement that the CRF is identical to the Sequence Listing must be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) and certain national stage filings; CRF may not be retained as part of the patent application file.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRF and late furnishing fee for international applications lacking ASCII listing
rubrics_metrics.description: If an international application lacks an ASCII plain text Sequence Listing and is to be searched/examined by US ISA/IPEA, the applicant must submit a CRF of the Sequence Listing, the late furnishing fee (§ 1.445(a)(5)), and a statement that the CRF does not go beyond the international application as filed or is identical, as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely provide required CRF may limit the extent of search/examination that can be meaningfully performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and opportunity to comply for missing Sequence Listing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If any of the Sequence Listing submission requirements are not satisfied at the time of filing or entering the national stage, the applicant will be notified and given time to comply to prevent abandonment; amendments must meet § 1.825 requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments adding/replacing Sequence Listings must follow the detailed amendment rules (§ 1.825).

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbols and format specifics for nucleotide sequences (pre‑ST.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nucleotide sequences shall use the lowercase one‑letter codes in Appendix A, be listed in groups of 10 bases except in coding parts, coding parts listed as triplets (codons) with corresponding amino acids immediately below, a maximum of 16 codons or 60 bases per line, single strand 5'→3' left to right, enumeration continuous starting at 1 appearing in the right margin, and circular sequences have optional first‑base designation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a codon spans an intron the amino acid symbol is listed under the portion containing two nucleotides; leftover fewer than 10 bases at line ends grouped together and separated by spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbols and format specifics for amino acid sequences (pre‑ST.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amino acids must use three‑letter abbreviations with the first letter uppercase (Appendix C), listed with a maximum of 16 amino acids per line, represented amino→carboxy left to right, enumeration conventions allow starting numbering at the mature protein (number 1) with preceding residues negative-numbered, internal terminators require separate sequences, and circular sequences allow optional first‑residue designation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amino acids preceding the mature protein (pre/pro sequences) can be numbered negatively counting backwards from the first mature residue; enumeration appears below every five amino acids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of sequences with gaps or noncontiguous segments (pre‑ST.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: A sequence with a gap or gaps shall be represented as a plurality of separate sequences, each with a separate sequence identifier; a sequence composed of noncontiguous segments or segments from different sequences shall be presented as a separate sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number of separate sequences should equal the number of continuous strings of sequence data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence Listing content and numeric identifiers (pre‑ST.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: The order and presentation of items in the Sequence Listing shall conform to appendix G; items designated with 'M' are mandatory; each item begins on a new line with the numeric identifier in angle brackets; include numeric identifiers <110> through <170> at the beginning; include each disclosed sequence; assign separate sequence identifiers starting with 1; use code '000' where no sequence present; include total number of SEQ ID NOs in <160>.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence Listing lines must not exceed 74 characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: PDF/paper Sequence Listing presentation requirements (pre‑ST.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Sequence Listing submitted as a PDF or on paper must begin on a new page, be titled 'Sequence Listing', include only the Sequence Listing, have sheets containing no more than 66 lines and no more than 74 characters per line, and should use a fixed‑width font and independent sheet numbering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These presentation rules help ensure machine readability and consistent pagination; exceptions apply for international stage per § 1.823(b)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: ASCII plain text file form/format requirements (§ 1.824)
rubrics_metrics.description: An ASCII plain text Sequence Listing and CRF may be created by any means but must be ASCII plain text, permit only printable characters and CRLF/LF line terminators, be named *.txt (filename rules: letters/numbers/hyphens/underscores only, <=60 characters excluding extension, no spaces), contain no more than 74 printable characters per line, and must be one continuous file with no pagination or hard page breaks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computer compatibility (PC or Mac) and OS compatibility (MS‑DOS, MS‑Windows, Mac OS, Unix/Linux) required; file size limits and submission media rules apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic and optical disc submission constraints for ASCII files
rubrics_metrics.description: ASCII plain text file must be submitted electronically via USPTO EFS where file must not exceed 100 MB and compression is not permitted, or on read‑only optical disc(s) in compliance with § 1.52(e) where compression (WinZip, 7‑Zip, Unix Zip) is permitted but self‑extracting archives are not and multi‑part split files must be labeled per § 1.52(e)(5)(vi).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not compressed, file must fit on a single read‑only optical disc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments adding a Sequence Listing after filing (§ 1.825(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any amendment adding a Sequence Listing after filing must include the Sequence Listing in compliance with §§ 1.821–1.824 (ASCII, PDF, or paper), a request that the amendment be made by incorporation by reference (for ASCII) or by inserting the Sequence Listing after the abstract (for PDF/paper), a statement indicating the basis for the amendment with specific references to parts of the original application, and a statement that the Sequence Listing includes no new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the added Sequence Listing is PDF/paper and a compliant CRF was not previously submitted, a new CRF and a statement that CRF equals the Sequence Listing must be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for replacement Sequence Listings (§ 1.825(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments that replace a Sequence Listing must include a replacement Sequence Listing in compliance with §§ 1.821–1.824 (labeled 'REPLACEMENT MM/DD/YYYY' if ASCII), a request for amendment by incorporation or insertion, a statement identifying the location of all deletions/replacements/additions, a statement indicating the basis for the amendment with specific references to original parts, a statement that the replacement includes no new matter, and a new/substitute CRF when required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If replacement submitted as PDF/paper and previous CRF missing or noncompliant, submit new CRF and statement that CRF equals the replacement Sequence Listing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of complete application to include incorporation paragraph (ASCII) (§ 1.825(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a complete application filed on the filing date includes a Sequence Listing as an ASCII plain text file but omits the incorporation by reference paragraph in the specification, the specification must be amended to contain the separate incorporation paragraph as required by § 1.77(b)(5), except for international applications during the international or national stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures the ASCII file is properly incorporated into the specification for U.S. prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: ST.26 XML Sequence Listing requirement for applications filed on/after July 1, 2022
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applications filed on or after July 1, 2022 that disclose nucleotide and/or amino acid sequences by enumeration of residues must contain, as a separate part of the disclosure, a computer‑readable Sequence Listing in XML format ('Sequence Listing XML') meeting §§ 1.832–1.834 requirements. Disclosed sequences not meeting the § 1.831(b) definition must not be included in the Sequence Listing XML.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence Listing XML must contain the sequences using symbols and format in accordance with WIPO Standard ST.26 as incorporated by reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of sequences for post‑2022 XML listings (§ 1.831(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: For post‑2022 submissions, sequences encompass (1) an unbranched sequence or linear region of a branched sequence containing 4 or more specifically defined amino acids forming a single peptide backbone, or (2) an unbranched sequence or linear region of a branched sequence of 10 or more specifically defined nucleotides (adjacent nucleotides joined by phosphodiester linkages or chemical bonds that mimic natural nucleic acids).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Specifically defined' is defined by WIPO ST.26 and 'amino acid' includes D‑ or L‑amino acids and modified amino acids as defined in ST.26.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence identifier assignment in Sequence Listing XML (§ 1.832(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each disclosed nucleotide or amino acid sequence that meets § 1.831(b) must appear separately in the Sequence Listing XML and be assigned a separate sequence identifier beginning with 1 and increasing sequentially by integers as defined in WIPO ST.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence identifiers in the XML must be used to reference sequences in the description/claims/drawings (preceded by 'SEQ ID NO:' or similar).

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation and symbols in Sequence Listing XML conform to WIPO ST.26 (§ 1.832(b)–(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Representation for nucleotide and amino acid data in the Sequence Listing XML must conform to the specific paragraphs of WIPO ST.26: nucleotide representation (paras. 11–12), symbols for nucleotides including analogs/modified/unknown (paras. 13–16,19,21), modified nucleotide descriptions (paras. 17–19), joint description of contiguous residues (para. 22), amino acid representation (paras. 24–25), symbols for modified/unknown amino acids (paras. 26–29,32), modified amino acid descriptions (paras. 29–30), joint description for contiguous 'X' residues (para. 34), and handling of constructed sequences, regions with specified numbers of unknown residues, and gaps (paras. 35–37).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule points applicants to the exact ST.26 paragraphs for machine‑readable, interoperable encoding of complex sequence constructs (noncontiguous constructs, gaps, repeats, modified residues).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence Listing XML file format and DTD validity (§ 1.833)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sequence Listing XML must be a single XML 1.0 file encoded using Unicode UTF‑8 (character set per WIPO ST.26) and must be valid according to the Document Type Definition (DTD) in WIPO ST.26 Annex II; it must include an XML declaration, a DOCTYPE declaration, and the required root element per ST.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conformance to ST.26 ensures the XML is syntactically and semantically valid for USPTO processing and international exchange.
